Asking Good Questions

For anyone who wants conversations to go deeper than small talk. Each day is one small way to ask a better question, follow up on an answer, and stay curious about the people around you, at home, at work and with new faces.

Communication · Communication · Relationships · one to-do a day · you choose how many days

Start this challenge free

The first seven days

  • Day 1Ask someone at home, "What made you smile today?" and simply enjoy whatever they share.
  • Day 2Greet a coworker or classmate with "What are you working on this morning?" and listen to the answer.
  • Day 3Listen to the end of one story today before you speak, then ask one small question about it.
  • Day 4Say hello to a neighbor you pass today and ask how their morning is going.
  • Day 5Remember a question someone once asked you that made you feel cared for, and enjoy that memory for a moment.
  • Day 6Swap "How was your day?" at dinner for "What was the best part of your day?" and see where it goes.
  • Day 7Ask one clarifying question before you start a task today: "What does done look like for this?"

Further into the year

The to-dos keep changing as the year goes on. A few from later in this theme:

  • Day 30Next time you want to ask someone a big question, check first that you both have the time and privacy for it.
  • Day 60Offer support by asking "What would be most helpful right now?" instead of guessing.
  • Day 120Gently ask yourself "Is this mine to fix?" when a worry feels heavy.
  • Day 240Notice when you are curious about someone and when you are just waiting to talk.
  • Day 365Keep a promise you made in a conversation, like passing along a name or a tip you mentioned, so the other person knows you listened.

How a challenge works

A Theraglee challenge is a theme with one small to-do for every day of a year. You choose how long yours runs, anywhere from a week to the full year, and each day you get the next to-do: something that takes a few minutes and fits inside an ordinary day. Tick it off when it is done. Nothing is scored and nothing is lost if you miss a day; the next to-do is simply waiting when you come back.

Challenges come with a free Theraglee account, which never asks for a card. Your progress stays private to you.
